title: Rabbi Tarfon's Hands
summary: One Shabbat, Rabbi Tarfon's mother's sandal tore, and he placed his hands under her feet with every step until she reached her bed. A warm, simple story about honoring parents, and about how there is always room to honor them a little more.
pages:
Rabbi Tarfon was a great sage. Many people came to learn Torah from him.
But there was something else special about him: he loved his mother very much.

One day, on Shabbat, Rabbi Tarfon's mother was walking in the courtyard.
The sun was warm, the birds were chirping, and she walked slowly, slowly, enjoying the Shabbat quiet.

Suddenly, rrrip! Her sandal tore.
The ground in the courtyard was hard and full of little sharp stones. How would she get home now?

Rabbi Tarfon saw and ran to her. On Shabbat you can't fix a sandal.
So what did he do? He bent down and put his hands on the ground, right under his mother's foot.

"Step on my hands, Imma," he said.
And so, step after step, she walked on the palms of his hands until she reached her bed. Her feet didn't get poked even once.

Some time later, Rabbi Tarfon wasn't feeling well.
The sages, his friends, came to visit him.

His mother said to them: "Please, pray for him. My son honors me far too much!"
And she told them about the sandal and the hands.

The sages listened, smiled, and said:
"Even if he did that a thousand thousand times, he still would not have reached half of the honor the Torah speaks of."

What does that mean? Even if Rabbi Tarfon did it a thousand times, and another thousand, and another thousand, it would still be only the beginning.
Because honoring your father and mother is such a big thing that it has no end.

And you? You can bring Imma a glass of water when she's tired, or hug Abba when he comes home.
Even little hands can do big things.
